newsitem.title: EGYPT: Irish cattle approach Egypt, may land despite ban.
newsitem.headline: Irish cattle approach Egypt, may land despite ban.

text.p: Three ships carrying about 4,500 Irish cows are approaching the Mediterranean port of Alexandria but cattle trade sources said on Wednesday Egypt would probably exempt them from a new ban on live cattle imports from Ireland.

The Galloway Express with about 1,600 cows aboard will enter Alexandria harbour overnight, about the same time as the Bison brings in slightly over 1,500 cows, the trade sources said. A third unnamed vessel is also on its way, they added.
Egypt imposed the ban on Monday after studying the latest data on bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) or mad cow disease. Government newspapers said it took effect on Tuesday.
In March last year the Irish government had to appeal directly to Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to let in Irish cattle ships stranded by a sudden ban on European beef imports.
The Egyptian veterinary authorities gave no signal of their plans for the ships on Wednesday but one trade source said the Irish exporters did not expect a problem this time.
"The receivers say there is no problem and the port is saying there is no problem. The situation will become clearer in the morning," said the source.
The new ban also covers live animal imports from France, Portugal and Switzerland, and all beef imports from Switzerland, the country most affected by BSE after Britain.
Egypt lifted Mubarak's ban on all European beef imports in April, restricting it to British beef. The new ban is valid for six months and will then be reviewed.
